prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a close-up kitchen layout with an upper wooden cabinet on the right at roughly 0.3 to 0.5 metres (brightest white) and an over-the-range microwave immediately to its left at 0.5 to 0.8 metres, both overhanging a recessed backsplash, stove control panel, and dark countertop below at 0.6 to 1.2 metres. In the lower-right foreground at about 0.3 to 0.5 metres—well within arm's reach of the camera wearer, who faces the counter and cabinet while tilting the head slightly right and downward across the five frames—the wearer's right hand holds a cylindrical object (pepper mill/shaker) in front of countertop bottles and a knife block. In frame 5, a second person's left forearm and hand enter from the lower-left edge at roughly 0.6 to 0.8 metres (about 0.4 metres left of the wearer's hand), reaching over a frying pan and foil-lined tray within their own arm's reach while the rest of both people's bodies remain out of view and no other person's face is visible or looking toward the camera. Across frames 1 to 5, the camera stabilizes from a tilted angle and shifts slightly backward in frame 5, exposing more of the lower counter and the bottles behind the wearer's hand. Compared to the dimly lit RGB image, the depth map clearly separates the overhanging cabinet and microwave plane from the recessed backsplash and isolates the foreground silhouettes of the hands, bottles, and paper towel holder, though it looks unreliable where the shiny black stove and dark far-left corner flatten into uniform black and where the held cylinder blurs into the wearer's fingers in frames 2 to 4.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map highlights selected regions of the kitchen scene across the first four frames, while leaving the rest of the layout—including the entire fifth frame, the second person's entering arm, and the wearer's held object—completely unsegmented. In frames 2, 3, and 4, a large green mask labeled 'microwave' covers the upper-right wooden cabinet door (roughly 0.3 to 0.5 metres in front of the camera wearer and within arm's reach), which sits directly above the counter and adjacent to the actual black microwave on the upper left (0.5 to 0.8 metres away). Below that cabinet in frame 4, a small cyan mask labeled 'bottle' at the bottom edge (about 0.5 to 0.6 metres away, just behind and to the right of the wearer's right hand) captures the neck of one countertop bottle that is partly occluded by the frame boundary and the wearer's hand. While this bottle mask helps isolate a dark glass bottle that blends into the shadowy backsplash in RGB, the map is largely unreliable throughout the sequence. In frame 1, it mislabels the wooden cabinet, wall, and wearer's hand as a sprawling pink 'person' mask and misclassifies the stove control panel and foil tray (0.7 to 1.0 metres away on the lower left) as a 'remote', in frames 2 to 4 it shifts the 'microwave' label onto the adjacent wooden cabinet door, and in frame 3 it hallucinates a 'keyboard' mask over the stove panel and pan.
descriptions.pose: The pose map renders sparse 2D skeletons on a black background, showing no visible heads or torsos facing or looking toward the camera wearer because both the wearer's body and the second person's body are outside the camera's field of view. Across frames 1 to 4, it completely misses the camera wearer's right hand holding the cylindrical container in the lower-right foreground at 0.3 to 0.5 metres (within the wearer's arm's reach). Instead, in frames 1, 3, and 4, it places erratic yellow body-joint skeletons over the lower-left stove control panel, frying pan, and foil tray (roughly 0.6 to 1.0 metres in front of and to the left of the wearer), and entirely omits all keypoints in frame 2. Only in frame 5 does a reliable magenta hand skeleton appear in the lower-left foreground at roughly 0.6 to 0.8 metres from the wearer (about 0.4 metres left of the wearer's unplotted right hand), tracing the wrist and five outstretched fingers of another person's left hand as it approaches from the left edge over the pan and foil tray within that person's arm's reach. This magenta skeleton in frame 5 makes the individual finger joints and rightward orientation of the motion-blurred entering hand clearer than in the RGB strip, whereas the yellow body skeletons in frames 1, 3, and 4 are false-positive hallucinations triggered by kitchen appliances and shiny foil.
